title: Chirurgie des surfaces conformes : notes manuscrites (s.d., 1983-1984), lettres (1984).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. The notes concern 'surgery' (chirurgie) of conformal surfaces. One starts from holomorphic pieces X''' (or X'') carrying pairs of disjoint discs (D'_i, D''_i) around points that are to be glued together. Removing the discs and gluing the boundary circles, with identifications coming from the pairing (in modern terms, plumbing zw = t at the nodes of a stable curve), produces a Riemann surface X. X has boundary, or marked points x_alpha, if discs D^k_alpha around marked points are also removed. The images Γ_i of the gluing circles are simple closed curves in X. By Thurston's principles each Γ_i determines a unique closed geodesic of the hyperbolic metric, though Γ_i itself need not be geodesic.

The problem on this page. Grothendieck asks whether the resulting X is independent of the choice of the disc pairs. He gives a heuristic he himself calls 'tout à fait vaseux' on the previous page. Replace D'_i by λD'_i and D''_i by (1/λ)D''_i, with λ in R_{>0} close to 1. This keeps the product of the radii, i.e. the modulus of the plumbing parameter. One then gets 'neighbouring (linearised) relations' for the discs in X''. He suggests one would obtain the same glued surface X, with the Γ_i replaced by neighbouring circles Γ'_i. He immediately adds 'c'est probablement tout à fait faux !'.

Key case: (g,ν) = (0,4). He then isolates the 'key case to understand' as (g,ν) = (0,4): gluing two Thurston pairs of pants.
- Fix two 2-element sets ε', ε''.
- Take pants of combinatorial type ε'⊔{s} and ε''⊔{t}, glued along {s,t}.
- The data are boundary lengths (l_i) for i in ε'⊔ε''⊔u, an element of (R_{>0})^{ε'⊔ε''⊔u}, where u indexes the glued curve.
- An element θ of the circle group U_{ε',ε''} fixes the gluing, i.e. the twist.

This is exactly Fenchel–Nielsen data for a four-holed sphere. He wants the function from these data 'vers' (towards) something. The next page indicates the target: groups of generalized parallels attached to ε'⊔{B}, ε''⊔{B}, and identifications in a Γ*-type object. In other words, the conformal/plumbing description of the same surfaces.

Purpose. The goal is to compare two parametrisations near a maximally degenerate stratum:
- hyperbolic pants-gluing data (lengths and twists);
- conformal surgery data (discs and gluing parameters).
The next page then asks for the induced map on fundamental groups of MD_g → M_{g,ν}, in terms of 'special Teichmüller groups'. This is the Esquisse-type programme of building the Teichmüller tower from the (0,4) and (1,1) pieces via pants decompositions.
errors: The heuristic about rescaling (λ, 1/λ) is flagged by Grothendieck himself as probably false. In the pure plumbing model it is actually harmless. If the gluing of the boundary circles is the restriction of a holomorphic identification zw = t, then cutting at radii λr', r''/λ instead of r', r'' gives the same Riemann surface, with Γ_i replaced by another circle in the same collar. The real difficulty is when the discs are defined by data that are not concentric in a common local coordinate, or when the gluing is only of boundary circles without an underlying holomorphic collar. In that case the conformal structure genuinely depends on the choices, and the independence claim is not justified.
The statement that the Γ_i are probably not geodesic is correct: plumbing circles are only close to the hyperbolic geodesics, asymptotically as |t| → 0.
Not an error but a gap: no actual comparison between (l_i, θ) and the conformal gluing data is carried out on this page.

ideas.what: Gluing Riemann surfaces along pairs of discs with rescaling λ, 1/λ preserving the gluing modulus; the glued curve should only depend on the product, with the cut circles moving within the collar.
ideas.modern_name: Plumbing construction / plumbing coordinates at the boundary of moduli space
ideas.usually_credited_to: Kra, Earle–Marden, Fay, Bers (1970s–1990); Wolpert for metric comparisons

ideas.what: Reducing understanding of gluing to the case (g,ν) = (0,4): two pairs of pants glued along one curve, with lengths l_i and twist θ in the circle group.
ideas.modern_name: Fenchel–Nielsen coordinates for the four-holed sphere; (0,4) as a building block of the Teichmüller tower
ideas.usually_credited_to: Fenchel–Nielsen; Thurston; Grothendieck's Esquisse (role of (0,4) and (1,1)); Hatcher–Thurston, Hatcher–Lochak–Schneps
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984), §§ on the Teichmüller tower, where (0,4) and (1,1) are singled out

ideas.what: Comparison map from hyperbolic pants data (lengths, twists) to conformal surgery data near maximally degenerate strata (MD → M_{g,ν}).
ideas.modern_name: Comparison of Fenchel–Nielsen and plumbing coordinates near the Deligne–Mumford boundary

missed.claim: Grothendieck explicitly sets up a comparison between Thurston's pants-gluing data (lengths and twist in U) and his conformal 'surgery' gluing of discs, isolating (0,4) as the key case. This links the hyperbolic and algebro-conformal descriptions of the degeneration that underlie the Teichmüller tower of the Esquisse. Later literature does make this comparison (Kra, Wolpert), but without Grothendieck's tower/Galois motivation.
missed.quote: Le cas-clef à comprendre sans doute est celui où (g,ν)=(0,4), i.e. la connaissance des recollements des deux "pantalons" de Thurston
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is mostly of historical interest: it shows Grothendieck trying to make the Esquisse's tower explicit analytically via pants-to-plumbing comparison. The mathematics itself is now known.

deep.surprise_reason: The page contains a self-doubted heuristic and the identification of (0,4) Fenchel–Nielsen gluing as the key case. Both are consistent with the Esquisse and with later standard work on plumbing versus Fenchel–Nielsen coordinates. There is no finished new result.
transcription_corrections: Line 1 likely reads 'par un changement ...' rather than 'pair un changement'; the text continues '..., si on remplace D'_i par λD'_i, donc D''_i par (1/λ)D''_i, avec λ ∈ R^{*+} voisin de 1'.
'linéarisées' is written above the line as an insertion, after the struck-out 'des'.
Probably 'donc pour deux ensembles ε', ε'' à chacun deux éléments, fixés, les fonctions de' (the two 2-element label sets), not 'donc [?] pour ... à chaque deux [?] éléments'.
In the brace, the index set is ε'⊔ε''⊔u, where u indexes the glued curve; the target is written (R^{*+})^{ε'⊔ε''⊔u}.
U_{ε',ε''} is almost certainly the circle group (twist parameter) attached to the gluing, written with a double-struck U.
The final word 'vers' begins the description of the target of the map, which continues on the next page.
